context.question: For 0 < p ≤ 1 < q, is the polygon bound exact for every finite spectrum and attained by a single exponent-one function of the observable?
context.locator: Pitchford, Conjecture 7.7 and Proposition 7.5, release v0.1.0-candidate
context.experiment: Enumerate every polygon chain for integer spectra and exponents, then solve the difference constraints exactly. Save labels; verify each pair. Audit every ordering for a small obstruction.
context.known: Author proves three levels in this regime. The literal q < 1 single-function clause fails on a 3–4–5 triangle; it leaves this q > 1 target open.
context.scope: A proof for all finite spectra or one certified counterexample to either prediction settles the stated conjunction. A failed monotone fit alone is insufficient. A strict distance failure requires a bound against the full cut cone.
